name: 27261-batchdecode-nemotron30ba3b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of one a3 node.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One engine, one GPU, no sharding of any kind.
architecture: hybrid NemotronH decoder (NemotronHForCausalLM), 52 layers: 23 mamba2 mixers, 6 attention, 23 MoE MLPs; ModelOpt FP8 weights, 30.44 GiB over 10 shards. Full config on the checkpoint.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=256, warmup 1.5625% (20 of 1280), cooldown 5%, bounded at 1280 requests with an 1800 s safety cap, static seed 27261.
workload: synthetic_text, single turn, `request_format: plain`, temperature 0: every request is exactly 1024 prompt tokens and exactly 1024 output tokens (min=max on both), EOS ignored. Prompts are Faker-generated synthetic English, freshly sampled per request.
purpose: A long-form writing assistant on one GPU, generating 1024-token drafts from 1024-token prompts for 256 concurrent users.
launch:
model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8

tensor-parallel-size: 1
pipeline-parallel-size: 1

# Twice the 256 streams the client offers, so the scheduler is never what limits concurrency.
# On a hybrid model this is also the memory knob: vLLM sizes the mamba state pool by
# max_num_seqs and not by context length, so 512 slots is ~23.5 GiB of pool -- the dominant
# term after the weights.
max-num-seqs: 512

max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
enable-chunked-prefill: true

# The worst case is 1024 prompt + 1024 output, so the window is not binding; it sizes the
# attention KV pool.
max-model-len: 3800

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9
swap-space: 16

# Inert at this commit: NemotronHConfig and NemotronHForCausalLM are both in-tree, so the
# repo's own modeling files are not executed. Kept because it costs nothing.
trust-remote-code: true
